linkedin.title: Class 1: What Is a Robot? Sense–Think–Act, Autonomy, and a Hands-On Python Lab
linkedin.description: Start your robotics journey with a clear definition of robots and autonomy, then build intuition for feedback, latency, and stopping distance. Apply it in a Python gridworld with manual vs. simple autonomous control.
linkedin.commentary:
What actually makes a machine a robot? In Class 1 of Professor OS, we ground the answer in the sense–think–act loop and show how autonomy relies on feedback, not magic. We begin simply, then add technical depth: reaction distance, stopping distance, and how latency (τ) and deceleration shape safety.

Highlights
- Clear taxonomy: machine vs. robot; autonomy vs. automation (and why gray areas exist)
- Practical math: v×τ for reaction distance and v²/(2a) for deceleration distance, with realistic caveats
- Hands-on lab: steer RoboRover manually or watch a simple policy navigate obstacles; measure bumps and reaction cells
- Accessibility and reproducibility: high-contrast mode, headless rendering, and seed control
- Real-world tie-in: how 2D lidars and ultrasonic sensors set loop rates and detection limits

Ready to try it? Run the Python lab, toggle obstacle density, and measure how performance changes. Then connect the gridworld to real robots by thinking in units, margins, and loop timing.
